annotations.text:
Report visual polish — aspirational targets.
Three report archetypes plus a chart-theme spec, all built from the same section vocabulary (kpi, chart, table, filter, markdown, download). Everything shown maps to a section the spec already has, except where a note says otherwise. Series palettes are CVD-validated against their surfaces (light and dark). Sample data is fictional.

Dashboard: KPI band + chart grid.
Filters dock in one row (max 3), the KPI band answers first, then a 7/5 chart row, a full-width trend, one table. Bars sort value-descending with direct value labels and rounded caps; the multi-series line carries a legend, end labels and a gradient area under the lead series. Proposed additions to today's renderer: side-by-side section widths (7/5 split), KPI delta captions, and KPI tile sparklines (each needs a small trend query) — all flagged for the design pass.

Narrative report: markdown-led single column.
A generate_report composition that reads like a document: serif prose with a drop cap, a hero KPI, figures sized to the text measure, numbered figure labels, and a compact table. Everything here exists in the contract today (markdown + kpi + chart + table + download) — the polish is measure, rhythm, and the centered paper surface.

Dense operational view: the table is the report.
Compact header, filters, a divider-strip of six KPIs (not six cards), a small-multiples strip (same measure, per-panel scale, one hue), then a dense grid sorted by urgency. Amber ink is reserved for state: the overdue KPI and the 7-plus-day overdue counts (the column tint is aspirational — table cells render plain text today). Deal names carry medium weight so the eye lands on the entity first.

Chart theme: where each styling decision lives.
Verified against the real code: the Lowdefy EChart block accepts a full theme OBJECT (properties.theme — it calls echarts registerTheme per block), but ECharts merges a theme UNDER the option, and flint's compiled option pins the stock palette and per-series itemStyle.color. So: palette + mark styling land in buildFlintOption's existing post-pass (it already rewrites barWidth, pie radius, legend), and one shared theme object carries typography, axis chrome and tooltip styling for every EChart the module renders — report sections, chat cards, expand modal.
